# onpager_routing_settings (Resource)

Manage the tenant's complete default routing recipient for alerts unmatched by all team/service filters.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "default_team_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "UUID of the active team receiving unmatched alerts."
}

resource "onpager_routing_settings" "example" {
  default_route = {
    target_kind = "team"
    target_id   = var.default_team_id
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `default_route` (Attributes) Complete fallback recipient. Used after enrichment only when no team or service filter matched. Omission or null clears the default; unmatched alerts then remain unassigned. Setting a service also assigns its owner team. The target must be active in this tenant when written; saved inactive targets remain readable. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--default_route))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Singleton identity and import ID: literal tenant. Configure only one owner per tenant.

<a id="nestedatt--default_route"></a>
### Nested Schema for `default_route`

Required:

- `target_id` (String) Known team or service UUID; names are not looked up and targets are not discovered. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.
- `target_kind` (String) Recipient kind: team or service.

## Import

Use the literal ID `tenant`. Import reads the current route, including null,
without modifying it. Configure only one owner of these settings per tenant.
Create refuses a nonempty unowned default route, even if it matches configuration;
import it explicitly before applying.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_routing_settings.example
  id = "tenant"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_routing_settings.example tenant
```

## Lifecycle

The default recipient is evaluated after enrichment, only when every team and
service filter yields no assignment. A service recipient also assigns its owner
team. These settings do not change existing alert assignments. The API validates
that a configured target belongs to the tenant and is active when written.
No target discovery, preview or alert admission occurs during CRUD.

Omitted or null `default_route` means no default recipient. An empty route remains
owned settings in Terraform state; it is not a missing resource. Saved routes to
inactive targets remain readable; routing runtime reports their unavailability.

Writes replace the complete route with an unversioned PATCH. There is no public
revision or `If-Match` protection: concurrent writes apply in commit order.
Refresh adopts route drift and a later apply reconciles configuration. Successful
mutation receipts populate state directly; a malformed successful receipt retains
the known submitted route with a diagnostic. Mutations are not retried.

Destroy clears the route through explicit `default_route: null`. It does not
restore any earlier UI snapshot or disable/delete the target. Failed clears
retain state. All read errors, including HTTP404, retain this always-existing
tenant settings object. An empty route leaves unmatched alerts unassigned.

## Permissions

Requires tenant `routing_settings.read` for refresh/import and the creation
ownership guard, and `routing_settings.update` for create/update/destroy.
PATs and native service accounts require explicit grants. Ordinary team/service
configuration grants do not imply these tenant settings permissions.
